ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Friedrich Nietzsche Synthetic CCD

text.paragraph: Establishing primary care for frequent disabling headaches with nausea and light sensitivity: headache history and red-flag screen, a headache diary, disability and mood screening, the daily combination tablets, MRI and syphilis serology, his eyes and his sleep. Concerns: Headaches on most days that stop him reading and writing, despite moving between climates to escape them; He fears that a brain illness like the one that killed his father may lie behind the headaches; Very poor sight in the right eye and tired eyes when reading; Short, broken sleep. [S]

Chronic migraine without aura (15 or more headache days a month for more than three months, at least 8 with migraine features); ICHD-3 criteria met in a two-week diary; MRI of the brain normal; synthetic modern diagnosis linked to his documented headaches, which historians interpret differently: active, confirmed [S]

Medication overuse headache from a butalbital, acetaminophen and caffeine combination on 10 or more days a month for more than three months, with ibuprofen on other days; resolved after a three-week taper and withdrawal: resolved, confirmed [S]

High myopia in both eyes, much worse in the right eye, since early childhood, with long-standing poor vision in the right eye and unequal pupils; comprehensive eye examination booked: active, confirmed [S]

Pathologic (degenerative) myopia of the right eye with patchy chorioretinal atrophy of the macula, a posterior staphyloma and a tilted optic disc; no choroidal neovascularization on OCT; best corrected vision 20/100 in the right eye: active, confirmed [S]
Chronic insomnia, with difficulty falling asleep and early waking, worse on headache nights; no sleep medicine at intake: active, confirmed [S]

Acute posterior vitreous detachment of the right eye, with flashes and a floater, without a retinal break, detachment or vitreous hemorrhage on dilated examination, in an eye with pathologic myopia: resolved, confirmed [S]

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Diagnosis: a structured headache history, a red-flag screen (SNNOOP10) at every visit, a 14-day diary of headache days, attack features, triggers and every dose of acute medicine, and ICHD-3 criteria; MRI of the brain with and without contrast because the headaches have become more frequent over the past year, are strongly right-sided, and come with long-standing unequal pupils and a very poor right eye; treponemal and nontreponemal syphilis serology because of past gonorrhea, unequal pupils and poor vision
Neurology (headache medicine) consultation to confirm the diagnosis and advise on withdrawal of the overused tablets and on preventive treatment

Medication overuse at intake: explain how frequent combination tablets can keep headaches going; count every tablet and acute-medicine day in the diary; take no more than now and never more than four combination tablets a day until the consultation; no new sedatives or sleeping tablets

Comprehensive eye examination for high myopia: refraction, pupils, pressure, a dilated fundus examination for myopic degeneration, retinal breaks and lattice, and macular OCT; correction of the large difference between the eyes; the warning signs of retinal detachment and an Amsler grid; dilated examination every year

Withdrawal: stop ibuprofen and replace as-needed butalbital combination tablets with a scheduled three-week taper (twice a day, then once a day, then every other day), because barbiturates are tapered rather than stopped abruptly; warn about rebound headache in the first one to two weeks and about the rare risk of withdrawal seizures; start prevention at the same time

Acute treatment after withdrawal: naproxen with metoclopramide early in an attack, no more than two days a week; sumatriptan added once the taper is complete, with no more than eight triptan days a month; no butalbital, opioids or combination products with caffeine

Preventive treatment for chronic migraine: galcanezumab 240 mg loading dose, then 120 mg monthly, judged at three months (at least half as many monthly migraine days); topiramate not chosen because of its effects on word-finding and concentration and its rare acute myopia with angle-closure glaucoma, a poor fit for a writer with high myopia; erenumab not chosen because of his constipation; onabotulinumtoxinA, every 12 weeks, as the next option or an addition
Sleep: cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia through the clinic's behavioral sleep program, a fixed rising time, a wind-down hour, and no sedative sleeping tablets
Mood: PHQ-9 and GAD-7 at intake and at about two to three months, with direct questions about hopelessness and self-harm at each visit; a safety assessment if a score or answer calls for one

Reading, writing and walking: good light, large print and an enlarged screen, breaks every 30 minutes, voice dictation for long passages, sunglasses and a brimmed hat for glare, and his daily walks kept as a protected part of the plan
A two-week headache diary and the tests that allow a firm diagnosis
Diary of 14 days kept; ICHD-3 criteria for chronic migraine and medication overuse headache met; MRI normal; syphilis serology nonreactive
Three-week taper completed a week before the four-week review; no withdrawal seizure or delirium; withdrawal headache settled within ten days
Fewer than 15 headache days a month, and at least half as many migraine days, within three months of starting prevention
At eight weeks: headache days 20 to 7 and migraine days 12 to 4 in the past four weeks; the three-month review is due
Acute medicine on no more than eight days a month after withdrawal
Acute medicine on 5 days in the past four weeks; no butalbital or combination product since the taper
Clear vision in the left eye for reading and protection of the right eye
Contact lenses fitted; left eye 20/20 and right eye 20/100 corrected; knows the warning signs of retinal detachment
Six and a half hours of sleep on most nights without sleeping tablets
Five and a half to six hours at eight weeks with CBT-I under way

list.item: Independent in all activities. On headache days he cannot read or write and lies in a darkened room, often vomiting; on other days he can read for about an hour at a time before his eyes tire. Headache disability: MIDAS 74 (grade IV, severe) over the past three months; HIT-6 68 (severe impact) [S]
Alert, courteous and precise, with a dry humor; speech normal; mood tired and frustrated by lost working days; thought organized; PHQ-9 7 with item 9 scored 0, GAD-7 6; no thoughts of self-harm [S]
